quals-berkeley-2024s-a01.prompt:
Differentiate
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+1&\text{if }x>1,\\ 2x&\text{if }x\le1.\end{cases}$$
Carefully explain, using the definition of the derivative, what happens at $x=1$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a01.answer: $f'(x)=2x$ for $x>1$ and $f'(x)=2$ for $x\le1$; at $x=1$ both one-sided difference quotients tend to $2$ (using $f(1)=2$), so $f'(1)=2$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a02.prompt:
(a) Give an example of a sequence of $C^1$ functions $f_n:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, $n=1,2,3,\dots$, and a $C^1$ function $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ such that:

(i) $f(0)=f_n(0)=0$ for all $n$,

(ii) $f_n'(x)\to f'(x)$ for all $x$ as $n\to\infty$, and

(iii) the following statement is not true: $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for all $x$ as $n\to\infty$.

(b) State a (reasonably general) extra condition which would imply that $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ for all $x$ as $n\to\infty$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a02.answer: (a) $f=0$ and $f_n(x)=\int_0^xg_n$ where $g_n$ is the tent of height $n$ on $[0,\frac2n]$: $f_n'=g_n\to0$ pointwise but $f_n(x)=1$ for $x\ge\frac2n$. (b) E.g. $f_n'\to f'$ uniformly on each $[0,R]$ (or dominated convergence: $|f_n'|\le g$ with $g$ locally integrable).

quals-berkeley-2024s-a03.prompt:
Let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function satisfying the mean value inequality below:
$$f(c)\le\frac1{2h}\int_{c-h}^{c+h}f(x)\,dx\qquad\text{for all }c\in\mathbb R\text{ and all }h>0 .$$

(a) Prove that the maximum value of $f$ on any closed interval $[a,b]$ is assumed at one of the endpoints.

(b) Prove that $f$ is convex.

Note: a function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is convex if $f(tx+(1-t)y)\le tf(x)+(1-t)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$ and all $t\in[0,1]$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a03.answer: (a) If the maximum $M$ were attained only inside, take the smallest maximum point $c\in(a,b)$; then $f<M$ on $[c-h,c)$ and the average over $[c-h,c+h]$ is $<M=f(c)$. (b) Subtract the chord (affine functions satisfy the inequality with equality); a point above the chord would give an interior maximum on $[a,b]$ exceeding the endpoint values.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a04.prompt:
Let the function $f$ be analytic in the entire complex plane and satisfy
$$\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|\,d\theta\le r^{17/3}$$
for all $r>0$. Prove that $f$ is the zero function.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a04.answer: Cauchy's formula gives $|a_n|\le\frac{1}{2\pi r^n}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(re^{i\theta})|\,d\theta\le\frac{r^{17/3-n}}{2\pi}$; let $r\to0$ for $n\le5$ and $r\to\infty$ for $n\ge6$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a05.prompt:
Let $f$ be the meromorphic function on $\mathbb C$ defined by
$$f(z)=1+\frac1z+\frac1{z^2}.$$
Use the argument principle to show that
$$\int_C\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz=0$$
for all positively oriented simple closed contours $C$ in $U:=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|>1\}$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a05.answer: $f=\frac{z^2+z+1}{z^2}$ has a double pole at $0$ and two simple zeros at the primitive cube roots of unity, all in $|z|\le1$. The closed unit disc lies entirely inside or entirely outside $C$, so $Z-P$ is $2-2$ or $0-0$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a06.prompt:
Let $M_{2\times2}$ be the vector space of all real $2\times2$ matrices. Let
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}\qquad\text{and}\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}$$
and define a linear transformation $L:M_{2\times2}\to M_{2\times2}$ by $L(X)=AXB$. Compute the trace and the determinant of $L$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a07.prompt:
Let $w$ be a positive continuous function on $[0,1]$, $n$ a positive integer, and $P_n$ the vector space of real polynomials whose degrees are at most $n$, equipped with the inner product
$$\langle p,q\rangle=\int_0^1p(t)q(t)w(t)\,dt .$$

(a) Prove that $P_n$ has an orthonormal basis $p_0,p_1,\dots,p_n$ (i.e., $\langle p_j,p_k\rangle=1$ for $j=k$ and $0$ for $j\neq  k$) such that $\deg p_k=k$ for each $k$.

(b) Prove that $\langle p_k,p_k'\rangle=0$ for each $k$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a07.answer: (a) Gram–Schmidt on $1,t,\dots,t^n$ gives $p_k\in P_k\setminus P_{k-1}$. (b) $p_k'\in P_{k-1}=\operatorname{span}(p_0,\dots,p_{k-1})\perp p_k$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a08.answer: (1)⇒(2): $u(v'-v'')=0$. (2)⇒(3): a unit is not a zero divisor (multiply by its inverse). (3)⇒(1): if $uv=1$ but $vu\neq 1$, then $w=vu-1\neq 0$ satisfies $uw=0$, so $v+w$ is a second right inverse.

quals-berkeley-2024s-a09.prompt: Classify all abelian groups of order 80 up to isomorphism.
quals-berkeley-2024s-a09.answer: Five groups: $\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_{16}$, $\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_8\times\mathbb Z_2$, $\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_4\times\mathbb Z_4$, $\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_4\times\mathbb Z_2^2$, $\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_2^4$ (one for each partition of 4).

quals-berkeley-2024s-b02.prompt:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, and let $\rho:X\times X\to\mathbb R$ be the function defined by
$$\rho(x,y)=\frac{d(x,y)}{1+d(x,y)}.$$

(a) Show that $\rho$ is a metric on $X$.

(b) Show that the metrics $d$ and $\rho$ are equivalent. (Recall that two metrics $d_1$ and $d_2$ are called equivalent if every convergent sequence in the metric $d_1$ converges also to the same point in $d_2$, and vice versa.)
quals-berkeley-2024s-b02.answer: (a) $\varphi(t)=\frac t{1+t}$ is increasing and subadditive, so the triangle inequality transfers. (b) $\rho\le d$, and $d=\frac{\rho}{1-\rho}\le2\rho$ when $\rho\le\frac12$; so $d(x_n,x)\to0\iff\rho(x_n,x)\to0$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-b03.prompt: Let $f$ be a continuous real-valued function on $[0,\infty)$ such that $\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ exists (and is finite). Prove that $f$ is uniformly continuous.
quals-berkeley-2024s-b03.answer: Choose $M$ with $|f-L|<\epsilon/2$ on $[M,\infty)$; $f$ is uniformly continuous on the compact $[0,M+1]$; with $\delta\le1$ any two points at distance $<\delta$ both lie in $[0,M+1]$ or both in $[M,\infty)$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-b04.prompt:
Let $f$ be an analytic function such that
$$f(z)=1+2z+3z^2+\cdots\qquad\text{for }|z|<1 .$$
Define a sequence $a_0,a_1,\dots$ of complex numbers by
$$f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty a_n(z+2)^n .$$
(Assume that the domain of $f$ is large enough, and connected.) Find
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}|a_n|^{1/n}.$$

quals-berkeley-2024s-b06.prompt:
Prove that the matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&1.00001&1\\1.00001&1&1.00001\\1&1.00001&1\end{pmatrix}$$
has one positive eigenvalue and one negative eigenvalue.
quals-berkeley-2024s-b06.answer: With $\epsilon=10^{-5}$ the characteristic polynomial is $x\bigl(x^2-3x-(4\epsilon+2\epsilon^2)\bigr)$; the quadratic has negative constant term, so its roots are one positive and one negative (the third eigenvalue is $0$).

quals-berkeley-2024s-b07.prompt:
A square matrix $A$ is nilpotent if $A^k=0$ for some positive integer $k$.

(a) If $A$ and $B$ are nilpotent, is $A+B$ nilpotent?

(b) Prove: If $A$ and $B$ are nilpotent matrices and $AB=BA$, then $A+B$ is nilpotent.

(c) Prove: If $A$ is nilpotent then $I+A$ and $I-A$ are invertible.
quals-berkeley-2024s-b07.answer: (a) No: $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}+\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ squares to $I$. (b) Binomial theorem: $(A+B)^{j+k}=0$ if $A^j=B^k=0$. (c) $(I-A)(I+A+\dots+A^{k-1})=I-A^k=I$; replace $A$ by $-A$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-b08.prompt: Show that any finite integral domain is a field.
quals-berkeley-2024s-b08.answer: For $a\neq 0$, $x\mapsto ax$ is injective (no zero divisors), hence surjective on the finite set $R$, so $ab=1$ for some $b$.

quals-berkeley-2024s-b09.prompt:
If $q$ is a rational number, the period of $q$ in base $n$ is the least number $a$ such that the base $n$ representation of $q$ eventually consists of a repeating sequence of length $a$. For example, the period of $1/7$ in base 10 is 6 since $1/7=0.\overline{142857}$.

Suppose $p$ is a prime number. Show that for any $n>1$ such that $p\nmid n$, the period of $1/p$ in base $n$ is at most $p-1$, and this maximum is achieved for some $n$.
quals-berkeley-2024s-b09.answer: The period of $1/p$ in base $n$ equals the multiplicative order of $n$ modulo $p$, which divides $p-1$; taking $n$ to be a primitive root modulo $p$ (e.g. a primitive root plus $p$, to make $n>1$) gives period $p-1$.
